item.title: MercoPress: The Spectator likens Milei's Falklands push to Galtieri's
item.description: An opinion column published on Wednesday in the British weekly The Spectator likens Argentine President Javier Milei's campaign over the Falklands to that of dictator Leopoldo Galtieri in 1982, with the difference, its author argues, that the current government is using legal rather than military means. The piece, by law professor Andrew Tettenborn, is an argument of opinion rather than a report of new facts.

item.title: MercoPress: London rejects Argentina's arbitration and questions its "reliability" as a partner
item.description: The British government has rejected Argentina's decision to initiate international arbitration over the Sea Lion oil project and said Buenos Aires' campaign over the Falklands "raises questions about Argentina's reliability as a partner for the United Kingdom". It is the first time London has extended the dispute to the bilateral relationship as a whole.
item.category: Energy & Oil, Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands, International

item.title: MercoPress: Trump and six tech companies sign a voluntary artificial intelligence safety accord
item.description: US President Donald Trump and the heads of six technology companies signed a voluntary accord at the White House on Tuesday under which the companies commit to ensuring the safety of their own artificial intelligence systems. Trump called it "morally binding" and said it was "almost like a constitution".

item.title: MercoPress: Pilot stabs another on a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight and passengers subdue him
item.description: A pilot on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv stabbed another pilot in the cockpit on Wednesday and, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, "apparently tried to crash the plane". Passengers and crew members subdued him, and the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk, in north-west Saudi Arabia, with all 174 passengers safe, 166 of them Israelis.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Venezuelan man shot by ICE in Texas is charged with assault
item.description: Wilber Rafael Garces-Perez is accused of striking an agent with his car's side-view mirror while driving away.

item.title: MercoPress: Foundering of Argos Georgia with the loss of 13 lives, MAIB report points to hatch failure
item.description: The marine accident investigation report refers to the loss of Argos Georgia, 23 July 2024, which occurred approximately 190 nautical miles east of Port Stanley. The Accident Investigation report 19/2026 includes what happened, subsequent actions taken and recommendations.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands Legislator meets PM Burnham and cabinet members at Liverpool
item.description: Falkland Islands Member of the Legislative Assembly Cheryl Roberts met and talked Monday evening with Prime Minister Andy Burnham and members of his ministerial cabinet in one of several receptions at the current Labor Party Annual Conference at Liverpool.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei opens Argentina Week at the OECD and will meet Macron at the Élysée
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei will lead Argentina Week in Paris from Wednesday, a gathering aimed at attracting European investment, with its main day on Thursday at the headquarters of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, ending that evening with a private meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace.

item.title: MercoPress: Lula remark on medical exams sparks controversy five days before the vote
item.description: A remark by Brazilian President and re-election candidate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva about men's reluctance to undergo prostate examinations has sparked a controversy in the final stretch of the campaign, after opposition figures linked it to child sexual abuse. Lula's campaign has taken the matter to the Superior Electoral Court.

item.title: MercoPress: A falsehood about Brazil's patron saint pits Supreme Court justices against each other mid-campaign
item.description: A false report that presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro backed stripping Our Lady of Aparecida of her title as Brazil's patron saint has produced contradictory rulings from three Supreme Federal Court justices, a clash with the Catholic bishops' conference and a dispute dominating the final week of campaigning before Sunday's vote.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina-Based Game Studio Releases New Game Based on The Walking Dead
item.description: When The Walking Dead comic began in 2003, few could have predicted what an incredible cultural phenomenon it would become. There have been countless TV spinoffs and various games as well.

item.title: MercoPress: Why Ethereum’s Dollar Value Matters as Latin America Expands Digital Payments
item.description: A designer in Montevideo can finish work for a company in São Paulo after the banks have closed. The transfer may involve two currencies, several providers and a wait before the final amount becomes clear. Stablecoin services offer a different route.

item.title: MercoPress: Latin American airports will need US$178 billion to nearly double their traffic
item.description: Airports in Latin America and the Caribbean will require investment of around US$178 billion over the next thirty years to handle demand that would rise from 809 million passengers this year to around 1.5 billion in 2045, according to projections presented in Lima at the annual assembly of Airports Council International.
item.category: Investments, Tourism, Latin America, Mercosur, Unasur

item.title: MercoPress: Milei orders arbitration proceedings against the UK over the Sea Lion project
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei on Monday instructed the foreign ministry and the government's legal teams to launch international arbitration proceedings against the United Kingdom over the development of the Sea Lion oil project in the basin north of the Falklands, and gave London two weeks to halt the activity before Argentina turns to the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea.
item.category: Energy & Oil, Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands, International

item.title: MercoPress: Chile's defence minister backs trade between Punta Arenas and the Falklands
item.description: Chile's Defence Minister Fernando Barros Tocornal has backed the development of commercial activity between the Magallanes region and the Falklands, saying his country's support for Argentina's sovereignty claim does not imply restrictions on trade with the archipelago. He made the remarks in an interview with Radio Polar in Punta Arenas during a visit to the region on September 24 and 25.

item.title: MercoPress: Lula widens his first-round lead to five points, but the runoff remains tied
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has widened his lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to five points in voting intentions for Sunday's first round, according to a Quaest poll released on Monday, though the two remain tied in a prospective October 25 runoff.

item.title: MercoPress: Five shipping lines warn Uruguay the port dispute is damaging its international standing
item.description: Five of the main shipping lines operating at the port of Montevideo have warned the Uruguayan government that the labour dispute at the Terminal Cuenca del Plata is causing "severe economic and commercial harm" and has "severely damaged Uruguay's international prestige", in a letter addressed to six ministers.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei denies a recession and says indicators are "throwing out anything"
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei denied the country is in recession and questioned the reading of statistics showing rising poverty and falling economic activity. "The indicators are throwing out anything," he said on Sunday in an interview with journalist Luis Majul on the programme La Cornisa, on the LN+ channel.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Argentina threatens legal action against UK over Falkland Islands oil exploration
item.description: President Javier Milei set a two-week deadline for the Sea Lion oilfield project to be scrapped.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Mexico's Pacific coast braces for Hurricane Polo
item.description: The category-four storm is approaching the state of Baja California Sur, on Mexico's northern Pacific coast.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Robbie Williams' surprise singalong after Peru gig cancelled
item.description: Robbie Williams gave an impromptu performance outside a hotel in Lima after his stadium concert was cancelled.

item.title: MercoPress: Chile reinforcing its military presence in Magallanes Region and Antarctica
item.description: Chile announced the reinforcement of its military capacities in the Magallanes Region, extreme south of the country with a plan that includes renewal of aircraft, modernization of armored vehicles, increased vigilance and presence in the austral territory and Antarctica, updating of military strategy based on experiences from the current war scenarios in Europe and Middle East.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands at Labour Conference in Liverpool
item.description: British political parties are holding their annual round of conferences and Labour, in government, has chosen the city of Liverpool for a gathering that started on Sunday, 27 September and will last for three days until 30th September.

item.title: MercoPress: The Telegraph links the Chagos deal to Argentina's Falklands campaign
item.description: An opinion column published on Sunday in the British newspaper The Telegraph argues that the decision to transfer sovereignty over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius served as a signal of weakness that encouraged claims over other British overseas territories, among them the Falklands. The piece, by journalist Daniel Johnson, is an argument of opinion rather than a report of new facts.

item.title: MercoPress: Britain has just received a painful reminder that nobody respects weakness
item.description: By Daniel Hannan (*) As the Chagos humiliation shows, the Foreign Office’s slavish adoration of international courts has got us nowhere. What has all our imagined soft power brought us? For all our performative internationalism, we find ourselves friendless.

item.title: MercoPress: London says Argentina “lacks the ability” to take the Falklands
item.description: British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said Argentina “lacks the ability” to take the Falkland Islands and that the United Kingdom “has the ability to defend” them, in an interview with the Sunday paper The Sun on Sunday published on Saturday. Asked whether London could protect the archipelago militarily if Buenos Aires sent warships, he answered yes.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Brazil's Lula bans online gambling ahead of presidential election
item.description: Lula, who is currently in a tight presidential race against Flávio Bolsonaro, said the industry was a "cancer" that he must "remove".

item.title: BBC Latin America: Venezuela releases dozens of political prisoners as election calls grow
item.description: A slew of dissidents being released from long-term detention comes days after the nation's interim leader met the US president.

item.title: MercoPress: Brazil reaches the election with its top court under suspicion and the candidates tied
item.description: Brazil votes next Sunday in a presidential election that arrives with the Supreme Federal Court mired in its worst institutional crisis since the return to democracy, the right's candidate formally under investigation in the same case, and the two leading contenders tied within the margin of error in every poll.

item.title: MercoPress: De la Espriella announces the reopening of oil exploration in Colombia, including fracking
item.description: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella announced on Friday that his government will "fully" reopen hydrocarbon exploration and the signing of new contracts, including hydraulic fracturing, during the swearing-in of businessman Joaquín Gutiérrez as president of Ecopetrol, the country's largest company.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands Assembly responds to Argentina's campaign: “This Assembly remains calm”
item.description: The chair of the Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly, Jack Ford, said on Thursday during a sitting of the body that there is “nothing new” in the claims made this week, and that the institution “remains calm” and steadfast in defending the right of the archipelago's residents to determine their own future.

item.title: MercoPress: The Falklands economic development agency appoints Josh Smith as managing director
item.description: The Falkland Islands Development Corporation, the archipelago's economic development agency, announced on Friday the appointment of Josh Smith as its new managing director, subject to final relocation arrangements. He will succeed Zachary Franklin, who will conclude his tenure in December.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei and Netanyahu discussed the Falklands in his only bilateral in New York
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for about twenty minutes on Thursday at United Nations headquarters, in what was his only bilateral meeting with a head of state or government during his trip to New York. Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno confirmed they discussed the Falklands.

item.title: MercoPress: “The UN has more reason to exist every day”, Uruguay's president said two days after Milei
item.description: Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi defended the United Nations' relevance and condemned the economic embargo on Cuba before the General Assembly on Thursday, in an address of just under twenty minutes that contrasted with that of his Argentine counterpart, Javier Milei, two days earlier from the same podium.
item.category: Politics, Argentina, International, Latin America, Mercosur, United States, Uruguay, Unasur

item.title: MercoPress: Poverty in Argentina rises to 32.3%, ending two years of decline
item.description: Poverty in Argentina reached 32.3% of people in the first half of 2026, an increase of 4.1 percentage points on the second half of 2025, the National Institute of Statistics and Census reported on Thursday. The figure interrupts the downward path the indicator had followed since mid-2024. Extreme poverty rose 1.2 points, from 6.3% to 7.5%.

item.title: MercoPress: Trump and Xi end the state visit with the trade truce extended and no substantive deals
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington ended on Thursday with a two-month extension of the bilateral trade truce, agreed before the meeting itself, and no progress on the central issues dividing the two powers: tariffs, rare earths, agricultural purchases, Taiwan and export restrictions on advanced chips.

item.title: MercoPress: Nine days from the vote, neither Brazilian front-runner comes close to 50%
item.description: Neither of Brazil's two leading presidential candidates is approaching the threshold needed to win outright on October 4, according to the latest Datafolha poll, which puts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on 40% of voting intentions and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on 36%.

item.title: MercoPress: Netanyahu rejects genocide allegations before an assembly emptied by dozens of delegations
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday called genocide allegations against his country over the war in Gaza "the biggest lie of the century", in an address to the United Nations General Assembly that dozens of delegations left before he began speaking.

item.title: MercoPress: Punta Arenas/Falklands maritime links are based on history, economics and geography
item.description: The announced maritime and trade link between Punta Arenas in Chile and the Falkland Islands has been strongly argued and supported by the main newspaper from the Chilean austral city on the Magellan Strait and capital of the Magallanes Region.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Venezuela‘s interim president promises election after Maduro ousted
item.description: The opposition in Venezuela has slammed her for not setting even a tentative date for elections.

item.description: The large storm in the Pacific Ocean is being driven by warm waters caused by the El Niño weather phenomenon.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Did El Niño turn Hurricane Polo into the most powerful storm of the season?
item.description: The BBC's Courtney Sargent explains how El Niño could have rapidly turned Hurricane Polo into one of the Pacific season's most powerful storms.

item.description: Canadian-Haitian writer Thélyson Orélien has just been awarded the Prix du Roman Fnac for his first novel.

item.description: The delivery driver was transferred from a hospital to a detention centre, his lawyer tells US media.

item.description: A report says the attacks, of which there have been at least 68, were not self-defence.

item.description: The suspects were flown to Miami to stand trial over the murder of Haitian President Jovenel Moise five years ago.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Watch: Aztec codex on display in Mexico for first time in 186 years
item.description: Mexicans celebrate the return of a centuries-old document that tells the story of the Aztec civilisation and its fall after the arrival of Spanish conquistadors.

item.title: BBC Latin America: New wild cat species discovered - with only one known living member
item.description: A spotted wildcat long mistaken for relatives has been identified as a new species in Bolivia.

item.description: Thousands of turtles arrived at La Escobilla beach in Oaxaca within 48 hours, sanctuary officials said.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Watch: Archaeologists discover ancient tomb in Peru
item.description: The burial site of the ancient pre-Incan Chimu culture was found largely intact.

item.description: Security camera footage shows a supermarket employee racing into action as a toddler runs towards moving traffic in Puebla, Mexico.

item.description: Haitian immigrants make up a large portion of the already overburdened home-care workforce.

item.description: With Argentina's President Milei promising "winds of change" over the Falklands, will Donald Trump shift his stance on British rule?

item.description: The WMO has warned that the natural weather phenomenon could bring disruption to global economies.

item.description: The 46-year-old figure of international intrigue has an apparent knack for being in the right place at the right time.
